approach: Fix both origins, keep liveness as one signal (registry entry or held job lock), and keep the noise down. (A) In the run: `Athena::dispatch` commits the job record and brief (run/mod.rs:1249-1257); any later `?` returns Err with no outcome, which `RealSteps::run` maps to `Run{outcome: None}` (drain.rs:4395-4408). Wrap the post-commit section: an error that is not a deliberate hold (LowDisk, SlotWait, BudgetShort), with the kill switch off, no resume mark, and the job still Dispatched at HEAD, closes the job `failed` through the existing `close_dispatched`. The reason now carries the existing `environment:` prefix (disk.rs:406), so the one classifier `StopCause::of` (disk.rs:469) reads it as `OtherEnvironment`: the scope guard does not count it (scope_guard.rs:544-551), `athena retry` may resume it (disk.rs:522-525), and the drain does not end its run on it (drain.rs:2589-2594 stops only for ProducerAuth, UsageLimit, LowDisk). Only invocations that left a trace are booked (`recover_traces`, split out of `recover_interrupted`; no synthesized producer). (B) In the listing: `steward::interrupted_work` keeps only the cli/steward channels (steward.rs:467) and hides every job that any later request retries (448-460), whatever became of that retry. Drop the channel filter for interrupted jobs only, reuse `reading::retries_by_job`, take liveness from a new `Athena::has_process(job)` (registry entry or held job lock; status.rs), and add a pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass, reported)` through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted` hook. The start pass only closes originals whose retry has ended; the final pass, after the sweep, also writes a `held <job>: <reason>` line for every dispatched job still without an outcome that the drain has not already named. `status` already lists every dispatched job without a process; its only change is that a job whose lock another process holds shows as running. The change is recorded as a new decision D167 in docs/decisions.md. Ordering: the six live jobs are closed or re-queued with today's `athena close` / `athena retry` BEFORE the new build runs its first drain.

A re-ask is not a retry for `retries_by_job` (reading/retry.rs:246-268), so msh3 and hvyb would be retried again and old web-channel jobs listed for the first time. Today's `athena close` already does what the six need. The first drain on the new build is bounded by `max_jobs`, the budget and ATTEMPTS = 2 per item (drain.rs:284), and the final pass names every job it does not reach.

decisions.choice: Close a job whose run errors after the Dispatch commit, inside `dispatch`, as `failed` with the reason `environment: stopped by an error after dispatch, before the job closed: <redacted error>`, via the existing `close_dispatched` with a `Closing` whose `new_invocations` come from `recover_traces`. The prefix is built from `crate::disk::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`; one `const` in run/mod.rs holds the text, and disk.rs is not edited. `close_after_error` returns the original Err (closes nothing) when: (1) the error downcasts to LowDisk, SlotWait or BudgetShort; (2) `state.registry().stopped()`; (3) `state.read_resume(id)` is Some; (4) the records reloaded at HEAD (`Records::load(&self.git, &self.head()?)`) show the job is no longer Dispatched; (5) the reload fails.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 3. An error that escapes `dispatch` after the commit is not a verdict on the work, because work failures close through `close_dispatched` normally (`finish_dispatched` calls it only on Ok, run/mod.rs:1342-1345). disk.rs:441-447 names `StopCause` as the one place that says which reasons are stops of the environment, and records that an unprefixed stop counted as a failure of the work, raised the retry, cost and time signals and paused the line. With the prefix: `StopCause::of` gives OtherEnvironment; `verdict_of` gives `Verdict::Environment` (scope_guard.rs:548-552), so T1, T2 and T5 do not count it; `resumable_stop` accepts it for `athena retry` (disk.rs:524); `settle_resume_marks` (run/mod.rs:871) would keep the job's own mark, and (3) means there is none. The earlier `stop_planning` precedent was a budget decision and is no longer cited. `failed` (not `abandoned`) is chosen because `athena retry` refuses an abandoned job (retry.rs:38-47) and `resumable_stop` accepts only failed-with-environment-reason. Condition (4) makes the guard explicit, so a later edit cannot produce a second outcome. `dispatch` holds the job lock, so `Athena::close` (manage.rs:96) cannot be called from there; `close_dispatched` can.

decisions.choice: New pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass, reported: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Vec<Settlement>` (`Close{job,why}` / `Hold{job,why}`) through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted(&self, final_pass: bool, reported: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Vec<String>`; `RealSteps` implements it with `Athena::close`. Population: `records.request_jobs()` in state Dispatched with `!live(job)`. Rules: (1) no request record (`athena retry` refuses it, retry.rs:54-56): Close 'dispatched with no request record; it cannot be retried', in both passes; (2) a standing retry followed through interrupted retries to depth 16, last retry closed: Close every interrupted job of the chain with `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`, in both passes; (3) `final_pass == false`: nothing else, never a Hold; (4) `final_pass == true` only: `held(job)` Some (disk or slot marker, `disk::read_any_hold`, run/mod.rs:481-490) or an open standing retry or no standing retry: Hold with a reason, except that a Hold is omitted for a job in `reported`. Hold text for no standing retry: 'dispatched with no outcome and no process; not worked in this drain (job limit, budget, stop, or its retry could not be read); `athena retry <job>` resumes it, `athena close <job> --why ...` closes it'.

The start pass cannot repeat an open-retry line on every drain. A pure function over `Records` is unit-tested without a model; a defaulted trait method leaves every test stub unedited, as `reclaim_interrupted` does (drain.rs:576). `Athena::close` recovers invocations, cleans and commits under the gate, and takes the job lock (manage.rs:96), so a live job is refused even if the probe raced.

risks.risk: The first drain on the new build retries every old interrupted job, the six included, and lists old off-channel jobs for the first time.
risks.mitigation: Operator step first: list every dispatched job with no outcome with today's `athena status`, close or re-queue the six with today's `athena close` / `athena retry`, close stale others with a stated reason, and only then deploy. The first drain is bounded by `max_jobs`, budget and ATTEMPTS = 2 per item, and the final pass names each job it does not reach.

risks.risk: The error close ends as failed a job that a later drain would have resumed, for example after a transient fault.
risks.mitigation: Only errors with no hold type, no kill switch, no resume mark and a job still Dispatched at HEAD are closed. The outcome is `failed` with an `environment:` reason, which `resumable_stop` accepts, so `athena retry` and the drain's second attempt can run it again. A hold or a built candidate stays dispatched.

risks.risk: A genuine fault of the work that raises an error after dispatch is classed as an environment stop and never counted by the scope guard.
risks.mitigation: Work failures close through `close_dispatched` on the normal path (run/mod.rs:1342-1345), not through this wrapper. The reason text keeps the error, so a person can tell. The bound is ATTEMPTS = 2 and no re-listing of a closed job, asserted by the drain test.

risks.risk: A later edit returns Err after a closing or blocked commit and the wrapper writes a second outcome.
risks.mitigation: `close_after_error` reloads the records at HEAD and returns the original error unless the job is Dispatched; a core test closes a job first and shows no second outcome is written.

risks.risk: Repeated failed retries of a request whose run errors the same way every time.
risks.mitigation: ATTEMPTS = 2 per item per drain, no re-listing of a closed job, MAX_RETRY_DEPTH 16, and a passed-over line. The drain test asserts at most two failed jobs, no new job from a second drain, and no pause or flag.

risks.risk: The drain retries or closes a live job another process runs.
risks.mitigation: `Athena::has_process` checks the registry and the job lock; it feeds the queue view, the settle and status. The settle's close goes through `Athena::close`, which takes the lock itself. A real-steps test holds the lock of an off-channel dispatched job with no registry entry and asserts it is neither retried, closed nor named in a held line.

risks.risk: The error close books a phantom producer at the producer cap.
risks.mitigation: The error close uses `recover_traces` only. The unit tests show no traces yield no invocation, and a test keeps `recover_interrupted` synthesizing the producer for `athena close`. No end-to-end claim is made.

risks.risk: The reason text of the error carries a secret or a machine path.
risks.mitigation: The reason goes through `ctx.redactor.redact` before it is committed; if redaction fails, a fixed text without the error is used. A core test puts a path in the error.

risks.risk: `close_dispatched` itself fails, so the job stays dispatched.
risks.mitigation: The original error is returned with the second as context. The next drain lists the job and the final-pass settle reports it with a reason.

risks.risk: Closing an original too early could lose work or retry it twice.
risks.mitigation: Settle closes only when the standing retry (followed through interrupted retries) has an outcome; an open retry gives a Hold at the final pass; a held job is never closed. Unit tests cover running, lock-held, held, open, closed and chained cases; a drain test asserts the retried original is not retried twice.

risks.risk: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing, so closing a middle job could re-list its parent.
risks.mitigation: The settle follows the chain and closes every interrupted job in it in one pass, depth cap 16. A Z-A-B unit test covers it.

risks.risk: Resuming off-channel jobs reverses a documented rule and an existing test.
risks.mitigation: The rewrite is explicit: D167, the CHANGELOG and the module doc name it. `queued_work` keeps its filter, pinned by a new test. The change applies only to dispatched jobs with no registry entry and no held lock.

risks.risk: Closing during a parallel drain races with a worker.
risks.mitigation: Settle errors become notes and never fail the drain. `close` takes the job lock and refuses a job another process runs. The final call comes after `sweep`, when all workers have finished.

risks.risk: Drain notes grow noisy.
risks.mitigation: Hold lines come only from the final pass, once per job, and never for a job in `reported` (already passed over or run by the drain). The start pass writes only Close lines, which happen once per original.

risks.risk: hestia.rs's private prefix constant drifts from the settle reason's literal prefix.
risks.mitigation: The literal is in one steward constant with a doc comment naming hestia.rs:342, pinned by a steward test; the effect of drift is limited to the review waiting for a newer introspection (hestia.rs:317-320). Residual risk accepted to keep hestia.rs out of the diff.

risks.risk: The `interrupt` helper leaves the history one commit short, unlike a real process death.
risks.mitigation: The helper is used only for the restart shape, and its tests assert before the drain that the job has no invocation and no outcome. The error-path tests use the real code path with a planner-role trigger and assert after the drain. `go_with_disk` (tests/drain.rs:2424) covers the hold case.

risks.risk: A planning-on Fixture builder in tests/drain.rs may need more scripting than expected.
risks.mitigation: If the Fixture cannot take the `[job_plan]` block as job_plan.rs:85 does, the drain-level error test is dropped and the core error test in run/tests.rs plus the `interrupt`-based drain tests carry criterion 1; the producer reports it.

risks.risk: The decision entry fails the D162 structure rule or the backtest link check.
risks.mitigation: The entry is appended after D166 as D167 with a Provenance bullet and avoids the words "superseded by", "supersedes" and "amends"; `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` and the full suite are run.

risks.risk: The six outcomes cannot be written by the diff because records/ is excluded.
risks.mitigation: The diff holds code, tests, CHANGELOG and the decision entry only. Demonstration 4 is an operator step with each close citing a hash read from git log; it needs write access to the live records.

risks.risk: Settle's `Athena::close` books a Missing producer at the cap for an original that never ran a producer.
risks.mitigation: This is what a person's `athena close` does today and keeps the cost bound honest for a dead process; noted in the CHANGELOG.

demonstrations.method: Four layers, each stopping a dispatched job before the producer runs and driving a production entry point. (1) Core: `Athena::go` with `repo_with_planning(1)`; the planner-role script plants the blocking `records` file so the first invocation fails after the Dispatch commit. (2) Drain, real steps: a cli job and a web job stopped with `interrupt` (asserted dispatched, with job.json and brief-producer.md, no invocation, no outcome before the drain), then `drain::drain`; and the planner-role error job in a planning-on Fixture, asserted after the drain. (3) A job whose lock is held with no registry entry. (4) steward `settle_*` and `interrupted_work` unit tests, plus the manage.rs `recover_traces` unit tests.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests::an_error_after_dispatch && cargo test --locked -p athena-core manage::tests::recover_traces && cargo test --locked -p athena-core steward::tests && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- interrupted after_dispatch
demonstrations.observes: Core: `go` returns Finished with state Failed and a reason starting `environment: stopped by an error after dispatch`; `crate::disk::is_environment_reason(&done.reason)` holds, `StopCause::of` is OtherEnvironment, `scope_guard::verdict_of` is `Some(Verdict::Environment)` and `resumable_stop` accepts the job; the job has job.json and brief-producer.md, a recovered planner invocation and no producer invocation; a low-disk hold, a kill-switch stop and a job already closed at HEAD are left as they were (original Err returned, no second outcome). manage.rs: `recover_traces` on a directory with no traces returns nothing; with a live record and a usage file it returns both; `recover_interrupted` still synthesizes the Missing producer for a job with no traces. Drain: the cli and the web original both end Closed(Abandoned) with a reason starting `re-queued as <retry>`; the planner-error job ends Closed(Failed) in the same drain with an `environment:` reason in the report, at most two failed jobs exist for the request, a second drain dispatches nothing, and `steps.paused`/`steps.flagged` return nothing for its line. The lock-held job is not retried, not named in a `held <job>` note and stays Dispatched. Steward: request-less is Close, closed retry is Close, open retry is Hold only when `final_pass` is true, dropped retry gives no settle but is listed by `interrupted_work`, running or lock-held gives nothing, chain Z-A-B closes both, `final_pass` false gives no Hold line, a job in `reported` gets no Hold line.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dispatch wrapper `go` returns Err and the job stays dispatched with no outcome, so the core and drain error tests fail. Without the new `interrupted_work` the web job is not listed and stays dispatched, a job whose retry was dropped is never re-listed, and a job whose retry landed stays dispatched. Without the lock probe the live off-channel job is retried and the lock test fails. Without the `environment:` prefix the `is_environment_reason` and `Verdict::Environment` assertions fail. Without the Dispatched-at-HEAD check, the unit test that calls `close_after_error` on a job already closed at HEAD writes a second outcome. The phantom-producer case is covered only by the `recover_traces` unit test, which fails if the synthesis moves into it.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs:402) and `drain::drain(&steps, limits(100.0), &Quiet)` with `RealSteps` from `real_steps(&athena, &lander)` (tests/drain.rs:4365, exists). demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- drain_leaves_no_dispatched_job drain_works_an_interrupted_item drain_notes_what_settling
demonstrations.observes: After the drain every request job is Closed, or is Dispatched and named in `report.notes` by exactly one line starting `held <job>:` with a reason and the `athena retry <job>` hint. The first job is retried and its original closed; the second is not worked and is held with a reason. A job the drain already passed over as held (disk-hold marker) gets no second `held` line. Stub: an interrupted item with an incomplete plan entry is retried (log `reread a`, `run a-retry`) with a note that the retry reads the request again; the start call (`final_pass=false`, `reported` empty) and the end call (`true`, `reported` = ids from `passed_over` and `st.jobs`) reach `Report::notes`; the start call never returns a Hold line. A job whose lock is held is not named in a held line.
